text:
Aisha: Quick idea — can we pilot a small "reminder runner" for postmortem actions? Owners often forget followups and we end up with stale tickets.
Kenji: Yes please. I've seen a few where the ticket was assigned but got buried. What do you mean by reminder runner?
Aisha: Lightweight: a weekly job that posts a thread into the postmortem channel and PMs owners for items past-due, with links and a suggested SLA for closure (e.g., 2 weeks for P1 remediations, 4 weeks for P2).
Marta: I like it. Could also include an explicit "owner handoff" step in the template so owners confirm within 48h or it escalates.
Liam: From product side: would be great to see recurrence patterns up-front. If an action is similar to a prior incident, we should surface that so we avoid duplicate engineering work.
Kenji: We should also align on comms cadence: who we CC, what constitutes a public vs private update. Maybe weekly summary in #incidents and owner pings in private.
Aisha: Proposal: 3 parts — (1) timeline template in postmortem (milestones + dates + owner), (2) reminder runner job, (3) escalation policy (no reply in 72h -> oncall lead gets pinged).
IncidentBot: Scheduled job registered: /reminder-runner every Monday 09:00 UTC — will DM owners for overdue actions.
Marta: For the timeline template, here's a minimal YAML snippet we can use in the pm doc:

```
timeline:
  - milestone: "Initial RCA complete"
    target_days: 3
    owner: "<name>"
  - milestone: "Action items assigned"
    target_days: 5
    owner: "<name>"
  - milestone: "First remediation review"
    target_days: 14
    owner: "<name>"
  - milestone: "Close and verify"
    target_days: 30
    owner: "<name>"
```

Kenji: That looks good. We should add a field for "related_incidents" so the runner can surface patterns (links to prior PMs).
Liam: +1 on related_incidents. Also can we attach a quick checkbox of "recurrence risk" (low/med/high)? helps prioritize.
Aisha: Implementation plan: Marta + Kenji build runner (small lambda / cron job) and UI is a simple post to channel + DMs. I can own the escalation policy writeup.
Marta: Will prototype the runner this week. Simple logic: query postmortem tracker (Confluence/Google Sheet) for open actions, check due dates, group by owner, post DM and thread. Example DM format: "You have 3 overdue items from PM #1234: [link], please update by Fri 23 Apr or reply with new ETA."
Kenji: For incident commander rotation, propose we publish the 6-week IC roster in the docs and the runner posts a reminder to next-IC 24h before their first shift.
Aisha: Nice. Let's also add a fast path for reassigning an owner in the runner: owner can reply "reassign @name" and the bot will create a follow-up action to the new owner (manual approval optional).
Liam: One more: add a small metric pulse to Console — % of actions closed on time, avg time to close. That will help product quantify improvements.
Marta: Agreed. I'll add a metric tag in the runner posts so our infra can pick it up.
Kenji: Slack PM content example for weekly summary: "Weekly PM reminders: X overdue actions, Y new actions, Z escalations — details: <link>."
Aisha: Ok next steps: Marta/Kenji prototype runner + timeline template by EOD Friday; I'll draft escalation policy and IC roster reminder rules; Liam will own metrics spec. 
Liam: Will do, adding a short spec to the incident process doc.
Marta: Ping me on the prototype if you want to test with a sample postmortem.
Kenji: I'll prep a small set of past PMs to test recurrence detection (3 examples).
Aisha: Great. If folks agree, I'll convert this thread into an action item and assign owners. :thumbsup:
Kenji: Agree. Thanks!
IncidentBot: Action recorded: "Pilot reminder-runner" assigned to Marta, Kenji, due 1 week from now.
